data.name: Hilleary
data.gender_notes: Hilleary is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek 'Helios' (sun) and 'Eirēnē' (peace), Hilleary signifies 'God's sunray of peace'. It was used in the early Christian era as a name for girls born to parents who wanted to honor the divine sun and symbolize peace. The name Hilleary carries the meaning “God's sunray” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Hilleary usually hope their child will grow to embody god's sunray and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A beacon of divine light and peace in the world.
data.etymology: Hilleary belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's sunray.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hilleary total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.
data.cultural_impact: Hanna, derived from the Hebrew 'hannah', meaning grace, became common in early Christian Europe as a girls' name and is now popular worldwide.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Bible, Hannah (1 Samuel 2:1-10) is a woman of deep faith and devotion who prays for God to give her a child. Her name continues to embody grace and faithfulness in Christianity.
